response.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, AVG(f.rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG((f.rebrate - f.feerate) / f.feerate) AS avg_rebate_vs_fee_ratio, AVG(f.rebtotal) - (SELECT AVG(f2.rebtotal) FROM fees f2 JOIN orders o2 ON f2.orderslink = o2.recordvault) AS diff_from_overall FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.ordertune HAVING AVG(f.rebtotal) > (SELECT AVG(f2.rebtotal) FROM fees f2 JOIN orders o2 ON f2.orderslink = o2.recordvault) ORDER BY diff_from_overall DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The 'overall average total rebate' is the average of rebtotal over all fee rows that match an order (after the inner join drops unmatched fees), ignoring NULLs.
Fees with feerate = 0 yield a NULL ratio in SQLite (division by zero returns NULL), so they are ignored in the ratio average, like other missing values.
orders.recordvault is unique per order, so the join does not duplicate fee rows.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average total rebate is computed over every row in fees, including fees with no matching order.
